text:
mike: ran nsys on the failing 2.3x throughput job on repro_v2. Timeline shows recurring ~900us CPU gaps where H2D memcpy completes then there's a ~1ms lull before kernel starts on the compute stream. Feels like copy-engine handshake/serialization, not pure kernel queueing. snapshot: https://artifacts/trace/2760012345/nsys.png
sophie: can you paste the cudaAPI timeline slice? is this on pinned or pageable?
mike: pinned buffer path (we pinned for prefetch). pasted waterfall snippet:
```
CUDA memcpy H2D (stream 2) 0.0-0.12ms
Kernel X (stream 1) 0.12-1.5ms
pause (cpu wake) 1.5-2.6ms
Kernel Y (stream 1) 2.6-3.9ms
```
that's simplified but shows kernel not launching until after host wake-up.
olga: are we seeing any hostspin in the runtime? maybe we fall back to synchronous copy due to pinned pool exhaustion
mike: good point — trace-bot shows occasional pinned allocation failures and a memcopy path switching to cudaMemcpy (blocking). nsys markers show copy_engine busy then cpu preempt.
raj: also check batcher heuristics: if microbatches end up with small seq lengths, we might interleave memcpys and kernel launches causing stream handshakes.
sophie: could be kernel selection too: we pick a kernel variant that uses different stream priority, forcing implicit serialization.
mike: yes, kernel selector switches to tiled-kernel on long context leading to higher shared memory and stream flags. timeline shows the kernel launch pushed to default stream implicitly (weird).
olga: action items: 1) reproduce with `NSYS_NVTX_SAMPLING=1` + perfetto to capture cpu-sched slices; 2) instrument batcher to tag NVTX with `batch_id` and `kvcache_hit`; 3) try forcing copy into async path using `cudaMemcpyAsync` on separate copy stream and pin a larger pool
mike: I already built a repro with envs: `REDWOOD_PREFETCH=1 REDWOOD_PINNED_POOL_SIZE=1G` and a small-run. attaching perfetto link: https://artifacts/trace/2760012345/perfetto.html
sophie: quick test — can you flip the copy stream to high priority (`cudaStreamCreateWithPriority`) and push prefetch onto that? If the stall disappears then it's scheduler ordering
mike: did that locally, delta looks promising: gaps reduce ~70%. But still see one-off 800us lulls when allocation spikes.
raj: hypothesis: pinned pool fragmentation triggers sync fallback which causes copy-engine to serialize and CPU scheduling to wait. Need hist of pinned alloc failures.
olga: also check kernel launch API ordering in code — make sure we don't call cudaDeviceSynchronize accidentally in error paths.
mike: grep found a `CHECK_CUDA_ERR(cudaStreamSynchronize(tmp_stream))` inside error handling path, but not in hot path. still will audit.
sophie: next steps: run an A/B with (1) increase pinned pool, (2) force async copy stream priority, (3) add NVTX for kvcache hits, and (4) microbench kernel variant selection disabled. I'll run cluster job tomorrow and post results.
mike: thanks — will add a small tracing PR to batcher with 3 NVTX tags and a short dashboard to visualize gaps. :raised_hands:
trace-bot: nsys trace uploaded: https://artifacts/trace/2760012345/nsys.qdrep
raj: if this is reproducible, we should consider a fast fallback in runtime: if prefetch hits pinned exhaustion then fall back to queued async copies rather than sync memcpy, or spill older kv entries earlier.
olga: agreed. Also file an incident if customer-facing perf regressed >10%.
